content.text:
Job description:
Graduate Analyst (London)

About the role
We are recruiting graduates into a twelve-month analyst programme in our business
analysis and reporting team, based in our London office. Analysts work with data
from across the business – sales, operations, customers and costs – to produce the
regular reports that managers rely on and to answer the questions they bring. The
programme rotates through reporting, commercial analysis and operations, and leads
to a permanent analyst post on successful completion.

What you will do
- Build and maintain the weekly and monthly reports in Excel and our reporting tools
- Pull together and clean data from the company's systems and spreadsheets
- Carry out ad hoc analysis for managers and explain what the numbers show
- Present findings clearly to colleagues who are not specialists
- Help improve how the team collects and checks its data

What we are looking for
- A degree in any discipline, achieved or expected at 2:1 or above
- Strong numeracy and confidence working with large spreadsheets
- Excel, and at least one query or coding language (such as SQL, Python or R)
- Experience of working with real datasets, from an internship, placement or project
- Clear written and spoken communication, including with non-specialists
- Accuracy under deadline pressure

Selection
Applications are screened on the CV, followed by a numerical test and two
interviews. Three in ten applicants are invited to interview at this stage.

Below are the CVs of the ten applicants in this screening round.

message.content: {"shortlist":false,"rank_in_round":4,"likelihood":35,"reason":"Felix is a strong 2:1 candidate with relevant customer-insight and research-assistant experience, but he narrowly misses the top three: Zoe and Marcus are clearly ahead, and Heather edges him for third because she evidenced SQL extraction from a live database and built an R script still in use, which maps more directly onto the role than his SPSS-based internship work."}
message.reasoning:
Zoe and Marcus stand out clearly as the top two, so now I'm weighing the third slot among Heather, Tom, and Felix. Felix has a 2:1 from York with internship experience analyzing survey data in SPSS and Excel, plus research assistant work in R, satisfying the coding/query language requirement even without explicit SQL. I'm now turning to Heather's 2:1 from Reading to compare her qualifications.

Heather has SQL and R experience, with her internship involving direct SQL pulls and a production R script, plus presentations to stakeholders — Tom also has SQL internship experience and presented his R-based dissertation to managers. Weighing it all, Heather's evidence of SQL and production-level work aligns more closely with the job's emphasis on pulling data from systems, even though Felix brings more breadth with two relevant experiences; I'm setting aside irrelevant details like school and hobbies, and landing on Heather third, Felix fourth with roughly 35% likelihood, and Tom fifth.
